comparator.name: Philosophy
comparator.sourceNotes: The current official 2026-2027 prospectus API reconstructs the full-time 180-EC Dutch-taught curriculum. The 60-EC first year and 30-EC second-year common core are compulsory. The normalized target does not name one of the four Dutch graduation specialisations, so Ethics and Political Philosophy is selected by the documented official-order tie break. For that route, Normative Ethics and Global Justice form the 20-EC second-year thematic selection; Advanced Moral and Political Philosophy plus Naming and Necessity form a valid 10-EC core-course selection; and Philosophy of Technology plus Metaethics form the 20-EC third-year thematic selection. A 10-EC thesis and 30 EC of genuine elective space complete the degree. The part-time programme is officially described as content-identical but paced over 4.5 years, so the full-time curriculum is the neutral normalized structure.

alternatives.distinctnessRationale: Compared with the closest match, this route replaces ten courses in archaeology, literature, general history and rhetoric with comparative politics, criminal and constitutional law, EU law, modern and contemporary sociology, environmental justice, gender history and an advanced history research seminar. The result prioritises normative public questions and institutions rather than broad philosophical and intellectual history.

comparatorRouteSelection.basis: The normalized target specifies the Dutch Philosophy bachelor but no graduation specialisation. The current official curriculum offers four equally formal Dutch routes and identifies no unspecialised completion route. Ethics and Political Philosophy is selected because it appears first in the current official curriculum, independently of UCR fit.

candidateAssessments.organisingLogic: The explicitly supplied candidate direction is “Ethics, politics and justice”; its interest-row basis and disposition remain explicit in interestSelection.

progressionAssessment.rationale: The schedule uses six four-course semesters from Fall 2026 through Spring 2029. Personal & Professional Development is in Year 1; all course offerings match the fixed cohort terms; none of the selected courses has an unmet formal prerequisite; and eight level-3 courses are concentrated in Years 2 and 3 after introductory philosophy, politics, rhetoric, history and interpretive work.

alternativeSelection.assessment: The broad closest match owns the general questions, historical breadth, argumentation and research interests. Two further generator-backed directions are coherent, feasible and materially distinct: ethics, politics and justice; and mind, language, knowledge and science. Their schedules differ pairwise by twelve to sixteen courses and all satisfy the hard constraints, so the maximum of three alternatives is reached.

comparisonAlignment.rationale: Both introduce foundational Western philosophical traditions, including ancient thinkers; UCR is a broader historical survey.
Both situate modern ideas in their historical context; UCR is general modern history rather than history of philosophy.
Both require sustained independent humanities research and a substantial evidence-based academic argument; UCR is a research seminar rather than a compulsory philosophy thesis.
Both develop close interpretation of historically situated texts; UCR is literature-focused and does not reproduce medieval philosophy.
Both develop normative ethical theories and reasoned evaluation of moral action; Leiden provides substantially greater specialist depth.
Both introduce major political-philosophical concepts and arguments; UCR is thematic rather than a dedicated historical survey.
Both develop political-theoretical analysis of authority, order and justice; UCR applies it to international relations.
Both examine justice and rights beyond the state; UCR approaches the topic through human-rights law and philosophy.
Both evaluate philosophical and ethical questions raised by contemporary digital technology and artificial intelligence.
Philosophy of Mind addresses knowledge, representation and mental states, covering part of Leiden’s broader epistemology component.
Both examine how experience, emotion and cultural frameworks shape human understanding; UCR is narrower and emotion-focused.
Both examine selfhood, time, agency and free will as metaphysical questions; UCR is a focused advanced seminar.
Both develop formal reasoning and validity; UCR combines logic with discrete mathematics and computing applications.
Both develop argument analysis, academic reasoning, writing, oral communication and critical engagement with claims.
Both analyse how language produces meaning; UCR focuses on style and rhetoric rather than analytic philosophy of reference.
Both require advanced argumentation about contested public and normative questions; UCR centres applied rhetoric.
Both examine competing traditions of interpretation and meaning; UCR is literary-theoretical rather than a history-of-philosophy survey.
Both address systematic inquiry and the status of evidence; UCR teaches qualitative methodology rather than philosophy of science.

notes.text: Leiden provides a continuous 180-EC Philosophy curriculum with dedicated sequences in ethics, logic, epistemology, metaphysics, philosophy of science, historical and comparative philosophy, advanced specialisation courses and a required thesis. UCR offers five dedicated Philosophy courses and builds the three alternatives with Politics, Law, Communication, History, Literature, Sociology, Cognitive Science, Psychology and AI. These are defensible interdisciplinary pathways but do not reproduce Leiden’s specialist disciplinary depth or required Philosophy thesis.
